narrative.overview:
Tiny Trips should feel like a well-thumbed local field guide a Vancouver parent keeps in the car: sea-and-forest colours, plain facts in a steady order, and real photos doing the selling. The palette comes from the place itself: deep Burrard Inlet teal for anything you can act on, and the blue-grey of a wet sky and damp cedar for everything else. Colour that means something (map pins, category dots) is the only bright colour on the page.

Density is practical, not airy. A parent on a phone, one hand on a stroller, should be able to scan a pin card in a second: photo, name, today's hours, ages, distance. Corners are almost square on purpose (2–6px), a deliberate step away from the over-rounded, bubbly look; only circles (pins, dots, the heart, the back-to-top button) stay round. Bricolage Grotesque gives headings a friendly, slightly hand-made voice; IBM Plex Sans keeps facts plain and legible.

Light and dark themes are both first-class. Dark mode is a deep forest-night floor, not pure black, and the main map uses its own dark vector style (only the fallback raster tiles are inverted).
keyCharacteristics: Map first: photo-led pin cards over the map, on a pale rain-sky page
Near-square corners; circles only for pins and dots
Category colour is meaning, never decoration
Soft neutral lift on cards and dialogs; everything else flat

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Inlet teal is the only interactive colour. If it's teal, you can press it.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Rule
rules.body: Category colours appear only on pins, type dots and category chips' dots. Never use them as decoration, section backgrounds or headings.

rules.name: The Shape-Backs-Colour Rule
rules.body: Any colour-coded mark also carries an icon or label; colour alone never carries meaning.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Bricolage for names and headings, Plex for facts. Never set hours, prices or ages in Bricolage.

rules.name: The Neutral Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are neutral ink, never coloured. No glows, no coloured halos, no radial colour washes behind content.

rules.name: The Readable-Count Rule
rules.body: Cluster numbers sit in their own layer above pins and below popups, never overlap each other, and shift up to 30px on screen to leave pin heads and the origin dot free. Don't fix crowding by grouping earlier.

rules.name: The Drop-Means-Ours Rule
rules.body: Only Tiny Trips places, events and markets use the drop shape. Base map icons stay round and dimmed.

rules.name: The Quiet Tag Rule
rules.body: Tags never get their own colour. If a tag needs to stand out, it isn't a tag: it's a warning (rose) or a selection (teal).

rules.name: The Square-Corners Rule
rules.body: Nothing above 6px radius except true circles. Over-rounded corners read as generic.

dos: Do use Inlet Teal for every pressable thing and nothing else.
Do keep corners at 2–6px; use full circles only for dots, clusters, the heart and back-to-top, and the drop shape only for our map pins.
Do pair every category colour with its line icon or a text label.
Do set names and headings in Bricolage Grotesque and facts in IBM Plex Sans.
Do use the neutral Card rest / Card hover shadows for lift.
Do design both light (Rain Sky floor) and dark (Night Floor) themes for every surface.
Do keep touch targets at least 32px for chips and 40px for buttons and inputs.
donts: Don't use coloured glows, coloured shadows or radial colour washes as backgrounds.
Don't round cards or buttons beyond 6px.
Don't use category colours as decoration or section backgrounds.
Don't put place-window sections in tinted boxes, pastel or grey. Separate them with a rule and space.
Don't introduce a second accent colour for actions.
Don't set body facts (hours, prices, ages) in the display font.
Don't use generic stock photos in the hero, or fade white hero text below full strength (the photo credit may be 95%).
Don't use emoji as icons (events, weather, categories, headings, badges). Use the line icon set (`typeIcon`, `wxSvg`, `evDot` in `app.js`); text symbols like ★ for ratings and ✓ are fine.
